demonstratedControlFlow: The guard is inside stopped_install after systemctl stop returned success and the original database owner lease was acquired exclusively. It is not the lease-acquisition refusal.
The predicate requires both ActiveState inactive and MainPID string zero; the reported guard alone does not identify which field failed.
Refusal precedes stopped financial re-audit, stopped ledger.sqlite backup, native-engine/service directories, new manifest/drop-in, current-release switch and new runtime start.
Before refusal, root bootstrap code/package directories, the immutable target release, verified before-stop backup and append-only preflight transition receipt have already been created.
Stopped-phase recovery releases the acquired database lease before requesting the original source restart. It does not restore or replace the ledger.
The recorded recovery phase proves successful start request, not subsequent runtime health.
preserveForRetry: Current original ledger, WAL, owner lock, all safe-stop/start/reconciliation/history/sequence changes.
Root prepared package/tools and immutable release; validate hashes before any reuse.
The before-stop verified backup and all append-only phase receipts.
Any stopped-phase partial files and actual systemd/journal evidence.
retryLimitations: Unchanged bootstrap refuses existing package/tools; unchanged upgrade also refuses an existing target release or transition. Do not delete evidence to rerun.
A reviewed continuation must validate exact prior refusal phase, original identity/funding, current flat unchanged financial obligations, indexed source bytes and actual stopped-process/cgroup state.
unknowns: Actual ActiveState/MainPID/ControlPID/Result/ExecMainCode/ExecMainStatus and cgroup members at the refusal.
Whether the original observer is presently healthy after its recovery start request.
An old observer SIGTERM callback can access the ledger after asynchronous close; a failed-but-dead exit is plausible, but not the established host cause.
